atAGlance: Crisp-fried fish with a golden crust, usually eaten with rice, herbs, and a lime-pepper salt dip or ginger fish sauce that cuts through the crunch.
whatItIs: Cá chiên xù is fish fried until the outside turns shaggy and crisp while the flesh stays moist. Depending on the restaurant, it may be served whole or as fillets.
usuallyIncludes: rice if ordered as a meal
howToEnjoy: Pull pieces of fish away from the bone or crust, dip lightly in lime-pepper salt dip or ginger fish sauce, and eat with rice and vegetables. A squeeze of lime keeps the fried coating lively.
howLocalsOrder: Cá chiên xù is ordered for crisp skin or coating, so ask whether it comes whole and whether bones remain. Locals use lime-pepper salt or a ginger fish-sauce dip to sharpen each bite.
worthKnowing: Vietnamese fried fish is often about contrast: hot crisp skin, clean white flesh, fresh herbs, and nước mắm or tamarind sauce rather than a heavy batter-only experience.
goodToKnow: Ask about bones before ordering, especially with whole fish. Crisp fish is best eaten hot, with herbs and a bright fish-sauce or tamarind dip if served.
